chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Bilal, from Al-Hasan ibn Bassam the Camelier, who said:

I was in the presence of Is'haq ibn 'Ammar the money-changer, so a man came seeking some grains for one Dinar. He had closed the door of the shop and sealed the bag, yet he gave him grains for one Dinar. I said to him, 'Woe be unto you, O Is'haq! Sometimes I carry for you from the ship thousands of thousands of Dirhams.' He said to me, 'I used to view it like this, but I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The one who belittles a little sustenance, would be denied a lot of it.' Then he turned towards me and said, 'O Is'haq! Do not belittle the little sustenance, for you would be denied a lot of it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of belittling small sustenance according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual principle of 'istikhlal' (underestimating small blessings) through the example of Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, a prominent merchant and companion of the Imams. It illustrates the Shia scholarly understanding that gratitude for minor provisions preserves major ones, linking material transactions to divine providence and the prevention of spiritual neglect.
